reference: Independent system ncurses tput in the mandatory isolated reference namespace, using the installed entries for all seven curated terminal names. Raw byte/status/tree evidence is retained. Custom query, sidecar, listing, info and variable binding are independent contracts, not GNU parity.
coverage: xterm control strings, colors and numeric capabilities
Terminal-specific attribute resets, standout modes, numeric absence and longname bytes across all seven curated entries
Parameterized capabilities with zero arguments (raw templates) and partial/full numeric arguments
Twelve common boolean capabilities, true/false status and empty output, across all curated entries
Leading -T, attached -TTERM, repeated overrides, -- and environment dimension behavior
Usage/missing TERM, unknown capability/terminal and known unavailable capability statuses
Custom sidecar escape decoding, parameter expansion, listing, info, -T selection and -V variable binding
exclusions: Metadata is excluded from operation coverage. Version/implementation identity is a custom contract, not an ncurses byte-equality requirement.
The curated data is qualified against the installed independent reference entries, not arbitrary compiled terminfo databases or user database replacements.
Only the twelve listed common booleans are supported; the complete standard/extended capability namespace is outside this suite.
init/reset terminal driver actions, serial padding timing, live dimensions, hardware and visible screen effects remain deferred.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash identifies tput as a builtin and its registered help is available, without invoking a terminal capability.
cases.script:
trap 'rm -f discard.out' EXIT
type -t tput
help tput >discard.out && printf 'help available\n'

cases.script:
TERM=xterm-256color tput cols
TERM=xterm-256color tput lines
TERM=xterm-256color tput colors
TERM=xterm-256color tput bold
TERM=xterm-256color tput sgr0
TERM=xterm-256color tput cup 2 4
TERM=xterm-256color tput el
printf '\n'
TERM=xterm-256color tput setaf 9

cases.purpose: Compare attribute reset and standout bytes, numeric values (including absent -1), and longname without a trailing newline across every curated terminal. Known absent strings return 1 with no output.
cases.script:
for term in xterm-256color xterm screen-256color tmux-256color linux vt100 dumb; do
 for cap in sgr0 smso rmso colors cols lines longname; do
  rc=0; TERM=$term tput "$cap" > "$term.$cap" || rc=$?
  printf '%s %s %s\n' "$term" "$cap" "$rc"
 done
done

cases.purpose: Compare terminal-specific clear bytes including scrollback clearing; dumb lacks clear and is checked in the error case. Output stays in isolated private files.
cases.script:
for term in xterm-256color xterm screen-256color tmux-256color linux vt100; do
 TERM=$term tput clear > "$term.clear"
done

cases.purpose: Compare unexpanded raw templates for every existing parameterized capability on all profiles, and no-output status 1 where VT100/dumb lack the capability. This qualifies per-profile data instead of copying xterm to every name.
cases.script:
for term in xterm-256color xterm screen-256color tmux-256color linux vt100 dumb; do
 for cap in cup cuu cud cuf cub sgr setaf setab hpa vpa ich dch dl il; do
  rc=0; TERM=$term tput "$cap" > "$term.$cap" || rc=$?
  printf '%s %s %s\n' "$term" "$cap" "$rc"
 done
done

cases.purpose: Compare cup with its missing second argument defaulting to zero, explicit zero coordinates, motion/edit counts, colors and profile-specific sgr evaluation.
cases.script:
for term in xterm-256color xterm screen-256color tmux-256color linux vt100; do
 TERM=$term tput cup 2 > "$term.partial"
 TERM=$term tput cup 0 0 > "$term.origin"
 TERM=$term tput cuu 3 > "$term.motion"
 TERM=$term tput sgr 1 1 0 1 1 1 1 0 1 > "$term.sgr"
 if [[ $term != vt100 ]]; then
  TERM=$term tput hpa 2 > "$term.hpa"
  TERM=$term tput vpa 3 > "$term.vpa"
  TERM=$term tput ich 2 > "$term.ich"
  TERM=$term tput setaf 4 > "$term.fg"
  TERM=$term tput setab 2 > "$term.bg"
 fi
done

cases.purpose: Compare true/false boolean statuses with no capability output for twelve common boolean codes across all seven profiles.
cases.script:
for term in xterm-256color xterm screen-256color tmux-256color linux vt100 dumb; do
 for cap in am bw xenl bce km mir msgr xon ccc hc npc hs; do
  rc=0; TERM=$term tput "$cap" > "$term.$cap" || rc=$?
  printf '%s %s %s\n' "$term" "$cap" "$rc"
 done
done

cases.purpose: Compare separate/attached/repeated -T and --, its override of TERM and dimension environment variables, and ordinary dimensions without -T.
cases.script:
TERM=dumb tput -T xterm-256color bold
TERM=dumb tput -Tlinux -Txterm colors
TERM=dumb tput -T linux -T xterm-256color -- colors
COLUMNS=99 LINES=33 tput -Txterm cols
COLUMNS=99 LINES=33 tput -T xterm lines
COLUMNS=99 LINES=33 TERM=xterm tput cols
COLUMNS=99 LINES=33 TERM=xterm tput lines

cases.purpose: Validate documented error statuses explicitly: 2 usage/missing TERM, 3 unknown terminal (before checking capability), 4 unknown capability. Diagnostic wording is intentionally unconstrained; stderr remains captured by the harness.
cases.script:
check_status () {
 expected=$1; shift
 rc=0; "$@" || rc=$?
 printf '%s\n' "$rc"
 [[ $rc -eq $expected ]]
}
export TERM=xterm-256color
check_status 4 tput no_such_capability
TERM=parity-no-such-terminal check_status 3 tput cols
TERM=parity-no-such-terminal check_status 3 tput no_such_capability
unset TERM
check_status 2 tput bold
TERM= check_status 2 tput bold
check_status 2 tput -T
check_status 2 tput -Q
check_status 2 tput -T xterm
TERM=dumb check_status 2 tput clear

cases.purpose: Known absent strings and false booleans return status 1, without output or diagnostics; explicitly validate each individual status.
cases.script:
rc=0; TERM=dumb tput sgr0 || rc=$?
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]
printf "%s\n" "$rc"
TERM=xterm-256color tput bw

cases.purpose: Preserve independent custom sidecar contracts: explicit -T and query -T selection, -V binding without output, cap-list, info, longname newline and sidecar expansion without arguments. A sidecar named xterm does not override a curated built-in entry, as before.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'name=Fixture' 'cursor=\E[%i%p1%d;%p2%dH' 'literal=A\nB\tC' 'cols=90' > custom
export BASHTPUT_TERMINFO_DIR=.
export TERM=dumb
tput -T custom cursor 1 2
printf '\n'
tput query literal -T custom -V value
printf '%s\n' "$value"
tput cap-list -T custom -V names
printf '%s\n' "$names"
tput info -T custom
tput -T custom longname
tput -T custom cursor
printf '\n'
printf '%s\n' 'bold=SIDE' > xterm
tput -T xterm bold
printf '\n'
entries=$(tput entry-list)
[[ $entries == *custom* ]]
printf "listed\n"
tput info -T xterm
tput info -T dumb
cases.stdout:
[2;3H
A
B	C
cursor literal cols
name=Fixture
cols=90
Fixture
[1;1H
[1m
listed
name=xterm
cols=80
lines=24
colors=8
name=dumb
cols=80
lines=24
colors=-1

cases.purpose: Custom query recognizes boolean aliases/status and rejects incomplete option operands with usage status 2; variable binding for ordinary capabilities remains supported.
cases.script:
tput query auto_right_margin -T xterm
rc=0; tput query auto_left_margin -T xterm || rc=$?
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]
printf '%s\n' "$rc"
rc=0; tput query bold -T || rc=$?
[[ $rc -eq 2 ]]
printf '%s\n' "$rc"
tput query bold -T xterm -V style
printf '%s\n' "$style"
tput query cup -T xterm -1 -2
printf "\n"
rc=0; tput cap-list -T parity-no-such-terminal || rc=$?
[[ $rc -eq 3 ]]
printf "%s\n" "$rc"

cases.purpose: Validate terminal-size queries and the visible effect of emitted control strings in a controlled PTY session.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or isolated PTY mock with a fixed xterm-256color terminfo entry, a controlled window size, and a terminal emulator/driver to observe the resulting screen state. The current harness captures stdout with no controlling terminal, so this integration behavior is not executed or counted as a pass.

cases.purpose: Full compiled terminfo loading, arbitrary user database replacements, aliases, extended capabilities and padding timing need separate implementation and qualification; this command intentionally preserves its custom text sidecar interface.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a version-pinned compiled terminfo database and independent ncurses reader. Arbitrary database parsing and padding timing are not qualified by the curated byte fixtures.
